title: Twenty Laughs Live
description: Twenty clean, room-friendly joke questions. Wrong answers are part of the fun; the last two are worth double points.

questions.question_text: Why did the scarecrow win an award?
questions.option_2: He was outstanding in his field
questions.explanation: He was outstanding in his field — standing in a field, outstanding at the job.

questions.question_text: What do you call cheese that isn’t yours?
questions.explanation: Nacho cheese. As in, ‘not yo’ cheese.’

questions.question_text: Why don’t scientists trust atoms?
questions.explanation: Atoms make up everything, so of course they can’t be trusted.

questions.question_text: What has many keys but can’t open a single door?
questions.explanation: A piano has plenty of keys and still won’t get you into the house.

questions.question_text: Why did the bicycle fall over?
questions.option_2: It saw a stop sign and panicked
questions.explanation: It was two-tired. Two tyres, too tired — pick your spelling.

questions.question_text: What do you call a bear with no teeth?
questions.explanation: A gummy bear. No teeth, all chew.

questions.question_text: Why can’t your nose be 12 inches long?
questions.option_1: It wouldn’t fit in a selfie
questions.option_2: Because then it would be a foot
questions.explanation: Twelve inches is a foot, and one nose per face is already plenty.

questions.question_text: What gets wetter the more it dries?
questions.explanation: A towel. The more it dries you, the wetter it becomes.

questions.question_text: Why did the coffee file a police report?
questions.option_3: It was too bitter to talk
questions.explanation: It got mugged. Baristas hear this one every morning.

questions.question_text: What do you call a fish with no eyes?
questions.explanation: Take the ‘i’s out of fish and you get fsh.

questions.question_text: Why did the student eat his homework?
questions.option_3: The teacher said it was a piece of cake
questions.explanation: If the teacher calls it a piece of cake, a hungry student may take that literally.

questions.question_text: What building has the most stories?
questions.explanation: A library. Storeys, stories — either way, the books win.

questions.question_text: Why don’t eggs tell jokes?
questions.option_3: The yolk would be on them
questions.explanation: They’d crack each other up, and breakfast would never recover.

questions.question_text: What do you call an alligator in a vest?
questions.explanation: An investigator. Vest on a gator. You’re welcome.

questions.question_text: Why did the banana go to the doctor?
questions.explanation: It wasn’t peeling well. A classic fruit checkup.

questions.question_text: What has a neck but no head?
questions.explanation: A bottle has a neck and still no opinions.

questions.question_text: Why did the golfer bring two pairs of trousers?
questions.option_2: In case of a hole in one
questions.explanation: In case of a hole in one. Golf jokes never go out of bounds.

questions.question_text: What do you call a boomerang that doesn’t come back?
questions.explanation: If it doesn’t come back, congratulations: you now own a stick.

questions.question_text: Why are ghosts terrible liars?
questions.option_2: You can see right through them
questions.option_3: Sheets have no pockets for notes
questions.option_4: They have nobody to back them up
questions.explanation: You can see right through them. Honesty is easier when you’re transparent.

questions.question_text: What’s the best day to cook chicken?
questions.explanation: Fry-day. The calendar’s funniest kitchen holiday.
